subject: BlueOrbit: Marketplace PO path & unit-econ next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: BlueOrbit discovery recap — marketplace purchase paths & unit-econ

Hi Elena — great conversation earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get procurement what they need.

Summary from call:
- Expected starting volume: 2–5M tokens/month, with seasonal spikes to ~12M in Q4.
- Primary requirement: predictable monthly unit cost and the ability to commit vs. overage.
- Preferred purchase path: marketplace private offer (AWS or GCP), but procurement asked to evaluate direct invoice if it yields materially better unit economics after marketplace fees.
- SLOs: 99.9% availability, p95 < 300ms for typical chat requests.

Unit-econ framing (high level):
- Redwood hosted list: $1,000 per 1M tokens (example baseline for illustration).
- Marketplace private offer math: marketplaces typically add a fee (we model ~15–22% depending on carrier). To keep equivalent net to Redwood we price private-offer list higher.
  - Example: to net $1,000/1M after a 20% marketplace fee, published private-offer unit price -> $1,250/1M.
- Direct invoice (subscription/commit) can often be offered closer to the hosted net (e.g., $980–$1,050/1M depending on commit tier) because no marketplace fee is applied.

Attached I’ve included a token_volume_breakdown.xlsx and a quick pricing-mapping CSV (pricing-mapping-aws-gcp-azure.csv) that shows three example scenarios: 2M/mo, 10M/mo, 30M/mo and how we map to marketplace private-offer list price vs direct invoice net.

Proposed concrete asks / next steps:
1) Confirm the monthly token commitment range BlueOrbit is comfortable with (low/typical/high months). That will drive whether we recommend 1-yr committed private offer vs month-to-month market listing.
2) Do you want us to draft an AWS private-offer price band (example: tiered per-1M unit price for 0–5M, 5–20M, >20M) so procurement can review in their PO template?
3) If procurement prefers marketplace PO, please loop them in so we can align on the PO fields they require (billing entity, payment terms, tax handling).

Next meetings: I propose a 30-min pricing alignment with procurement early next week. I can bring Vanessa (pricing/marketplace lead) and Sergio (deal engineer) to answer technical mapping questions.

Thanks — attaching the files referenced. If anything in the spreadsheet looks off, tell me and I’ll update.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: BlueOrbit discovery recap — worked examples & proposed bands

Elena / Procurement — thanks, cc’ing Vanessa for marketplace price band guidance and Sergio for technical mapping. Below are the worked examples you asked for and a recommended next step.

Worked examples (assume Redwood target net = $900/1M on committed volume):
1) Scenario A — 3M/mo committed, 20% overage:
   - Redwood net on committed units: $900 x 3 = $2,700 net/month.
   - If marketplace fee = 20%, published private-offer price to buyer = net / (1 - fee) = $2,700 / 0.80 = $3,375 total -> per 1M published = $3,375 / 3 = $1,125/1M.
   - Overage: if overage billed at the same published rate, buyer pays published $1,125/1M for overage. If we agree on higher overage premium (e.g., +10% published), overage published -> $1,237.50/1M.

2) Scenario B — 10M/mo committed, 10% overage:
   - Redwood net on committed units: $900 x 10 = $9,000 net/month.
   - Marketplace fee = 15% (GCP estimate) -> published = $9,000 / 0.85 = $10,588.24 total -> per 1M published ≈ $1,058.82/1M.
   - With tiered discounts we’d recommend published bands: 0–5M = $1,150/1M, 5–20M = $1,058/1M, >20M = $980/1M (published), which preserves net targets after fees depending on carrier.

Region / marketplace variance:
- Fees vary: AWS historically ~20% for private offer handling, GCP ~15%, Azure ~18% (these are modeled estimates; we can confirm exact percentages during offer creation). For split-region deployments we typically either:
  1) Centralize procurement in one marketplace billing entity (preferred) so one private-offer price applies, or
  2) Create two private offers split by region with slightly different published unit prices to reflect fee differences.

Attachments / artifacts included:
- token_volume_breakdown.xlsx (worked examples per month & annualized spend)
- pricing-mapping-aws-gcp-azure.csv (shows recommended published bands by carrier and the net per-1M after fees)
- redwood_po_template.docx (example PO fields we need: billing entity, pricing band, effective date, termination, contact, payment terms)

Suggested next steps (concrete):
- Procurement: review redwood_po_template.docx and tell us any mandatory PO fields or redlines.
- Redwood/BlueOrbit pricing alignment call: 30 mins Tue Apr 6 or Wed Apr 7. Proposed attendees: Logan, Vanessa, Sergio; Elena + procurement rep.
- If procurement confirms marketplace PO is acceptable, we will draft the AWS/GCP private-offer with the initial published band and send the formal quote.

I’ve uploaded the artifacts to the HubSpot deal record and included a DocuSign link for the sample PO (not final). Links below.

Thanks — I’ll hold Tue/Wed open for a short call.

Best,
Logan
